title: Your AI Agent for Your Existing Database: Retrieve, Update and Manage

sections.label: 1 - AN AI AGENT ON YOUR EXISTING DATABASE
sections.note: You ask your database a question in plain English. Claude reads your tables and answers from the real rows, never from memory.

sections.label: 2 - RETRIEVE, UPDATE AND MANAGE: UPDATES WAIT FOR YOUR YES
sections.note: Your parts 2 and 3: retrieving and updating in one smooth chat. A change is shown back to you as old value and new value first, and only a yes moves it forward.

sections.label: 3 - INTEGRATED WITH YOUR CURRENT DATABASE
sections.note: The approved change is written to your own Postgres, inside one transaction, only to the tables and columns you allowed. Every change lands in a change log you can undo from.

sections.label: 4 - RELIABLE PERFORMANCE: IF ANYTHING FAILS, YOU HEAR ABOUT IT
sections.note: A failed query or a timeout never fails quietly. You get an email with the step, the error and a link to the run.

nodes.label: 1 - You Ask Your Database in Plain English
2 - Claude Finds the Records You Asked For
nodes.notes: Answers come from your rows, with the IDs, so you can check any answer.

params.system_message: You are the database assistant for this company's existing Postgres database. Always answer from the search tool, never from memory, and include the IDs of the rows you used. If a search returns nothing, say so and suggest one looser search. When the user asks to change, add or archive anything, call the hold tool with the table, the row ID, the column, the current value and the new value, then show the old value and the new value and ask them to reply yes. Only the tables and columns listed in editable_tables can be changed; refuse anything else and say why. Never delete a row: archive it by setting status to archived. Set action to apply only when the user's latest message clearly approves the change you held in this chat; otherwise set action to answer. If two rows could match a change, list both and ask which one.

nodes.label: Claude - Reads Your Data and Plans the Change
Memory - Remembers the Chat and the Change Waiting for Your Yes
Tool - Search Your Tables · Read-Only
nodes.notes: Read-only: it runs parameterised SELECTs, so a question can never change a row.

params.description: Search the database. Input: table, filters as column and value pairs (for example status = pending, customer_name = Dana Whitfield), and a limit up to 50. Runs a read-only parameterised SELECT and returns the matching rows with their IDs.

nodes.label: Tool - Hold an Update, Add or Archive Until You Say Yes

params.description: Stage a change without applying it. Input: table, row ID, column, current value, new value and the reason. Checks the table and column are in editable_tables, reads the live current value, writes one row to agent_pending_changes with status pending and this chat's session ID, and returns the change_id with the old and new values to show the user.

nodes.label: Claude Writes the Reply and Says Answer, Confirm or Apply

schema.reply: Order 5521 for Dana Whitfield: status is Pending now, will be Shipped. Reply yes to apply.

nodes.label: 3 - Did You Say Yes to the Change?
nodes.notes: The guard: Claude can suggest a change, only your yes applies it.

nodes.label: 3b - Answer You, or Show the Old and New Value to Confirm
4 - Postgres: Apply the Staged Change to Your Live Row
nodes.notes: Applies only a change staged earlier in this same chat, only to the columns you allowed.

params.query: SELECT change_id, table_name, record_id, column_name, old_value, new_value FROM apply_agent_change($1, $2);

options.queryReplacement: ={{ $json.output.change_id }},{{ $('1 - You Ask Your Database in Plain English').item.json.sessionId }}

nodes.label: 5 - Postgres: Log What Changed, When and in Which Chat

params.query: INSERT INTO agent_change_log (change_id, table_name, record_id, column_name, old_value, new_value, chat_session, applied_at) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7, now()) RETURNING *;
